_exec_summary.SummaryText:
This RMP for the Campo Viejo Gas Processing Plant has been prepared in accordance with 40 CFR Part 68 and reflects a Program Level 1 classification for both covered processes. All required components for Program 1 facilities have been addressed, including worst-case release analysis, ERP coordination, and five-year accident history. Stakeholder Midstream is committed to continued safe operations, emergency preparedness, and RMP compliance.

A. Accidental release prevention and emergency response policies:
Stakeholder Midstream is committed to protecting the health and safety of its workers, the public, and the environment. The Campo Viejo site maintains systems and procedures to safely handle flammable substances, including internal programs for preventive maintenance, employee training, and safe operating practices. Although not required under Program 1, elements of OSHA Process Safety Management (PSM) are implemented. In the event of an incident, the facility follows a detailed Emergency Response Plan (ERP), which has been 
coordinated with local emergency responders. The ERP includes evacuation procedures, tiered response classifications, and clear communication protocols.

B. Stationary source and regulated substances handled:
The Campo Viejo Gas Processing Facility includes front-end liquids handling and gas compression, amine treating with acid gas injection, cryogenic processing, and nitrogen rejection. Natural gas liquids (NGLs) are stored onsite and routed to pipeline sales. The facility handles regulated flammable substances, including ethane, propane, butanes, pentanes, and heavier hydrocarbons, in quantities exceeding the EPAs 10,000-pound threshold. Hydrogen sulfide (H?S), a listed toxic substance, is present in process streams; however, process-specific 
inventory evaluations confirm it remains below the 10,000 lb threshold for RMP applicability for each train and the facility as a whole. Methanol is present in both storage tanks and process streams;

however, total inventory remains below the 10,000-pound RMP threshold, and it is not modeled as a separate covered process.

C. General accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps:
Although not required under Program Level 1, the facility implements key prevention practices aligned with industry best practices and OSHA PSM. These include:
   Preventive maintenance and routine inspections
   Safe work practices such as lockout/tagout and hot work permitting
   Training for operators and maintenance personnel
   Process hazard evaluations and incident investigations
The facility also uses alarms, automated isolation systems, and a flare system to manage toxic and heavier-than-air gas releases safely.

D. Five-year accident history:
Under 40 CFR §68.42, the five-year accident history requirement applies to releases of regulated substances from covered processes that were held above threshold quantities and resulted in on-site deaths, injuries, or significant property damage, or known offsite impacts such as deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering-in-place, property or environmental damage. Based on information provided by Stakeholder Midstream, no RMP-reportable accidental releases have occurred at the Campo Viejo Gas Processing Facility within the past five years. Campo Viejo Gas Processing Plant Risk Management Plan (RMP) Document No: 25-SM-860 Stakeholder Midstream 

E. Emergency response program:
The Campo Viejo site maintains a comprehensive ERP that satisfies the requirements of 40 CFR §68 Subpart E. The plan outlines procedures for fire, explosion, toxic release, and natural disaster scenarios. An Incident Management Team structure is used for coordination, and emergency notifications are made in compliance with EPA, TCEQ, PHMSA, and NRC requirements. The facility has coordinated the ERP with local emergency response organizations and ensures employees are trained in evacuation and shelter-in-place procedures. The most rece

nt review of the ERP was conducted on June 18, 2024.

F. Planned changes to improve safety:
No additional safety-related changes are currently planned; however, Stakeholder Midstream is committed to continual improvement and will review and enhance safety systems as part of ongoing process safety management and audit activities.
